clue.text: Make shorter drive with jazz fan into heart of Ostend

indicators.note: into says the other pieces are pushed inside the letters taken from Ostend
the heart of a six-letter word is its central pair of letters

parts.note: to drive a business or a car is to run it
a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut a trip short: a drive with a jazz-loving friend into central Ostend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes TE, the middle two letters of OSTEND; RUN and CAT go 'into' them.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate is to cut off the end of something, which makes it shorter.

clue.text: Accepted that, in French language

parts.note: something accepted or fashionable is in
the French word for that is ça, written CA in the grid

explanation.surface: Someone concedes a point while speaking French.
explanation.definitionFit: Inca is also used for the speech of the Inca people of Peru, the tongue now usually called Quechua.

clue.text: Frantic swallow perhaps claims highest spot

indicators.note: claims means the drink takes hold of the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a draught is a gulp or swallow of drink; 'perhaps' marks it as one example
first place, written 1ST, read as IST

explanation.surface: A swallow, the bird, frantically grabs the highest perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow perhaps' suggests a bird, but it is a gulp of drink. 1ST written with the digit read as the letter I is a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught and frantic are synonyms, both describing someone beside themselves with worry.

clue.text: A stand used for flower

parts.note: to stand for election is to run for it

explanation.surface: A display stand is used to show off a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, something that flows. The Arun is a river in Sussex, in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a flower is anything that flows, so a river such as the Sussex Arun qualifies.

clue.text: Defence system that's used in wrestling around ring

indicators.note: around means the wrestling item is wrapped about the ring letter

parts.note: wrestlers grapple on a mat
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A wrestler's defensive technique used around the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' tempts as the wrestling ring, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-filled ditch surrounding a castle served as its first line of defence.

clue.text: It's a minor problem extracting right shellfish

indicators.note: extracting means the letter for right is pulled out of the word

parts.note: a wrinkle is a small snag or difficulty to be ironed out

explanation.surface: A small complaint about having to pull something out of a shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A winkle is a small edible sea snail, sold as seafood in Britain.

clue.text: Country stream close to cottage in British Isles

indicators.note: in says the stream and the letter go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: BI is the abbreviation for British Isles
a run is a small stream, especially in American usage

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of cottage

explanation.surface: A rural scene: a stream running near a cottage somewhere in the British Isles.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places everything in the British Isles, but the answer is a sultanate on Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sovereign state on the north coast of Borneo.

clue.text: Again invest in road being rebuilt on banks of Rhine

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the rebuilt letters after the other piece
the banks of a river are its two sides, so the word's outer letters
being rebuilt says the letters of these two words are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Investing again in a road that is being rebuilt along the Rhine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' is not about money but about formally installing someone in a church office.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a priest is to install them in office, so ordaining a second time means investing again.

clue.text: Dick consumes roll with dark nuts — they're usually pickled

indicators.note: consumes means the detective swallows the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: dick is slang for a detective; DS is detective sergeant
a roll, as in being on a roll, is a run of luck

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of dark are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man named Dick eats a bread roll with some dark-roasted nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' looks like a name but is a detective, DS. 'nuts' turns DARK into KARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is slang for very drunk, so habitual heavy drinkers are typically in that state.

clue.text: Open University flying course latterly in news

indicators.note: in says the speedy word and the letter go between the two letters from news

parts.note: news read as N's, two Ns, N being the abbreviation for new
flying means very fast, as in a flying visit

indicators.note: latterly picks the last letter of course

explanation.surface: The Open University's fast-track course gets a late mention in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open University' reads as one institution, but 'Open' is the definition and only U is used. NEWS is taken as N's, two Ns, with FAST plus E between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a door or a coat is to undo it, which opens it.

clue.text: Clothing career in periphery of Kent repelled son

indicators.note: in says the running word sits between the two edge letters
repelled means driven back, so the edge letters are taken in reverse order
the periphery of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: to career is to run headlong

explanation.surface: A clothing career on the edges of Kent, from which a son was turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' reverses KT, the letters 'periphery of' takes from KENT, to TK. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Trunks are shorts worn for swimming or boxing, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Before joining a volunteer group, get rid of facial hair

indicators.note: before joining places the elimination word ahead of the rest

parts.note: to zap something is to destroy or eliminate it
TA is the Territorial Army, the British Army's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Advice to a recruit: shave off your moustache before signing up with the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer military reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zapata is a drooping moustache named after the Mexican revolutionary Emiliano Zapata.

clue.text: Football team agreed to continue on special diet

indicators.note: on joins the rearranged letters after the other pieces

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word for yes, signalling agreement
a play that continues is said to run

indicators.note: special signals the letters of diet are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A football team agrees to stay on a special diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges DIET into ITED. Ayr United is a Scottish football club from the town of Ayr.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr United is a professional football club based in Ayr on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Detainee here goes off commander probing another contingency scheme?

indicators.note: probing means the honour pushes into the middle of the scheme

parts.note: after plan B and plan C, yet another fallback would be plan D
KBE is Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A commander investigates yet another emergency plan after a prisoner escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' suggests an escape or alarm, but it means drops off to sleep, so the whole first part describes where a prisoner sleeps. Plan D follows plans B and C as one more fallback.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare wooden board serving as a bed in a cell is where a prisoner drops off to sleep.

clue.text: 1 to perform during training

indicators.note: during means the performing word comes in the middle of the training letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise training
a machine or program that performs is said to run

explanation.surface: A cross-reference instruction to act during a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' refers to the answer of 1 Down, which means make shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune a tree or a text is to cut it back, making it shorter.

clue.text: Reviewing satire, most of Sky edition showed highlights?

indicators.note: reviewing means looking over again, here going over the letters of satire in a new order
most of means all but the last letter of Sky

explanation.surface: A TV critic reviews a satirical programme from a Sky broadcast that showed highlights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reviewing' rearranges SATIRE into ASTERI; 'most of' cuts the last letter from SKY. 'highlights' is not the sports kind but items picked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking passages with a star symbol draws attention to them, picking them out as notable.

clue.text: Mock off-road vehicle that's right for Prince

indicators.note: R for P means the letter for right takes the place of the letter for prince

parts.note: a Jeep is a rugged four-wheel-drive car

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a prince's four-wheel drive, saying it is right for him.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or taunt someone with scornful shouts.

clue.text: Race dominated by car, a fuel-guzzler producing this noise?

indicators.note: dominated by means the racing word is held between the letters of the car

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a high-performance car, the sort that drinks fuel
to race is to run

explanation.surface: A race dominated by a gas-guzzling sports car, with its throaty engine noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a straining engine making a low guttural sound is a loose fit; the car in the wordplay doubles as the source of the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, deep, guttural sound, like that of a pig or a labouring engine, is a kind of noise.

clue.text: In auditorium, regret element of dressing

indicators.note: in an auditorium the audience hears the word rather than sees it

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Someone in a theatre regrets part of their costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests clothing or costume, but it is a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooked mix of flour and fat is the base for many sauces and gravies, so part of a dressing.

clue.text: Left-winger perhaps with foot swelling, heading off first

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the swelling is removed

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the joint of the big toe
first written 1ST, read as IST

explanation.surface: A left winger in football hobbles with a swollen foot and goes off first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-winger' suggests a footballer on the left flank, but here it is a politically left-leaning trade union member.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union member is typically on the political left, so an example of a left-winger.

clue.text: Punter briefly circles course seeing chestnut filly?

indicators.note: circles means the shortened gambler wraps around the course word
briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a punter is a gambler, one who bets
a run is a course, such as a ski run

explanation.surface: A gambler goes round the racecourse looking at a chestnut-coloured young mare.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing surface suggests a horse, but the 'filly' is a girl with chestnut hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Filly is informal for a young woman, and one with chestnut-brown hair is a woman with dark hair.

clue.text: Arm stretch embraces adult and young, abandoned

indicators.note: embraces means the stretch word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a run is a stretch, as in a run of good weather
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: abandoned means the word young is emptied, its inside left behind

explanation.surface: A long arm stretches out to hug an adult and an abandoned child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like a limb but is a weapon. 'abandoned' keeps YG, the outside of YOUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: A science-fiction beam weapon is a type of firearm, so an arm in the military sense.

clue.text: Art critic wanting to go off-piste in print?

indicators.note: in says the snow-sport word sits inside the print word

parts.note: a print run is the number of copies printed in one go
going off-piste means skiing away from the marked slopes

explanation.surface: An art critic who would rather be skiing off-piste than appearing in print.
explanation.walkthrough: John Ruskin was a leading Victorian English art critic.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin was the foremost Victorian writer on art, the champion of Turner and the Pre-Raphaelites.

clue.text: Greyish-beige ferrets you held back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are then read in reverse order
held says the letters are gripped within the two words, hidden there

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is warned that the ferrets have grabbed hold of them and won't let go.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'held back' to the reversal alone; 'held' is the hiding signal and 'back' the reversal, so both operations have their own words.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyster is a paint and fabric colour name for a pale greyish white, like the shellfish's inner shell.

clue.text: Operate while concealing current bankruptcy

indicators.note: concealing means the operating word hides the current letter inside it

parts.note: to operate a machine is to run it
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Running a business while hiding the cash flow that is leading to bankruptcy.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial ruin is the state of having lost everything, which is what bankruptcy brings.

clue.text: After pressure, hunt stops misuse of guns, like 14 Across?

indicators.note: stops means the other pieces plug a gap in the rearranged letters
misuse of means the letters of guns are mishandled into a new order
after places the chase word behind the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
a hunt or chase can be called a run

explanation.surface: After pressure, a hunt group stops gun misuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misuse of' rearranges the letters to UNSG. The cross-reference is to the prison sleeping board at 14 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden prison bed has no springs, the question mark showing it is one example of something springless.

clue.text: Luvvie regularly wiped a part of his eye

indicators.note: regularly wiped means every other letter is erased, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A theatrical type keeps dabbing away a tear from part of his eye.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a gushing actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigmented middle layer of the eyeball, including the iris, is a part of anyone's eye.

clue.text: Weakest Link to be broadcast on time

indicators.note: on joins the time letter after the broadcast word

parts.note: a TV series that is being broadcast is said to run

explanation.surface: The quiz show Weakest Link is to go out on air on time.
explanation.walkthrough: Weakest Link was a British TV quiz; here the words mean the feeblest of a litter.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest, feeblest animal in a litter is the weak point of the bunch.

clue.text: Tremble when catching daughter swinging vehicle

indicators.note: catching means the trembling word grabs the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to quake is to tremble
swinging is slang for bisexual, shortened to bi

explanation.surface: Someone trembles on catching their daughter swinging a car about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging' looks like a careless driving action but is slang for bisexual, BI.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled motorbike used off-road is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Chap finds home of East End woman?

indicators.note: of makes it the home belonging to her, so the woman's word comes first

parts.note: a Cockney from London's East End drops the H, so her becomes 'er
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A man discovers where a woman from the East End lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a working-class area of London whose Cockney accent drops initial H, so 'er nest is her home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so stands for any fellow.
